steps.text: Place bacon in a large skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon slices on paper towels.
Combine bacon, green beans, onion, butter, chicken broth, garlic, salt, and pepper in a saucepan. Cover and simmer on medium heat until beans are tender, 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Country Green Beans
raw_recipe.description: Fresh green beans are cooked with bacon, onion, and garlic for a delicious side dish.
raw_recipe.name: Country Green Beans

review.reviewBody: After I removed the bacon from the cast iron skillet, I left some of the bacon fat in the skillet and sauteed the beans, onion and a little fresh minced garlic in the bacon fat with a pat butter, added some fresh ground pepper and let it cook until the onions started to turn translucent. I then poured over the chicken broth and simmered. We LOVED these green beans. My husband said that these reminded him of beans his Dad made for him growing up, he was quite upset there weren't any more. Next time, I'll double the recipe.
Delicious green beans! I sauteed the onion and garlic in some of the bacon grease, then added the other ingredients to the skillet, only dirtying one pan. I only used about 1 TBSP butter.

This was wonderful, and I hate when people rate the recipe when they changed things, but *sigh*, I changed things slightly. I saved the cooked bacon until the green beans were done and then crumbled on before serving (so the bacon was still crispy), and I must have used about 3/4 a cup of chopped onion, I used 1 and a half cloves of garlic, and I used a full cup of chicken broth - half a cup to start and then the other half halfway through cooking because the pot looked a little low on fluid. They turned out great! Definitely a keeper.

I used all the same ingredients but changed up the cooking method. After steaming the green beans I rinsed them in cold water to cool and then drained. While I was doing that, I sautéed the onions in the butter and the seasonings then added the chicken broth. Once combined, I added the green beans and heated through. Before serving, I topped with the crumbled up pre-cooked bacon so it would still be crispy. I also had some grated Parmesan cheese on the table which some chose to use. We loved this recipe and a great winter comfort food. Definitely a keeper.

Everyone liked this. I left out the salt as I felt there was enough in the bacon. I threw everything but the broth in the pot and cooked on medium-low for 10 minutes, then added the broth and cooked 5 more minutes.

We love green beans with bacon and onion. I did this recipe a little different though. Fry up the bacon, remove and drain all the grease from the pan except what clings to the pan. Add the onions and saute them in the little bit of bacon fat - add the garlic and cook for just a minute or two then add the green beans and the chicken broth. Use the broth to deglaze the bacon goodness from the bottom of the pan. Cover and cook until tender. Plate the green beans and sprinkle with the reserved bacon. (The juice from the green beans is excellent added to gravy if you are making gravy.) This way you save the calories from the butter and only mess up one pan.
Like others added tbsp butter to bacon grease then sautéed onions garlic and beans then deglazed with chicken broth

I usually double this recipe and I use a bag of already trimmed fresh green beans from Costco. I stick the Bacon in the Freezer for about 30 min before chopping, so it's easier to cut into small pieces. I brown the bacon in a pan, then add shallots (instead of onions) and some fresh garlic. I remove everything from the pan and add the green beans in with the butter and a little olive oil. I cook until their cooked but still a little crisp, then add the other ingredients back into the pan and season with salt and pepper. I didn't include the chicken broth.

I make this dish often every summer as I always have a bumper crop of beans. At least once I really splurge and make it the old farmers way. Brown the bacon, remove bacon, discard all but 2 tablespoons of bacon fat (so would not use the butter in this recipe), saute the onions in the bacon grease and then add the bacon and the rest of the ingredients and cook until the beans are tender. The bacon grease really does add a sinfully good flavor. I only do that once or twice a summer. The rest of the time I make it as this recipe directs using Smart Balance margarine. It's really a wonderful veggie side dish.

I followed the recipe, but left out the butter and chicken broth. I didn’t see any reason to add butter when I had bacon grease. I used half of the bacon grease to fry the onions and garlic. Then I added the beans and a little water to keep them from burning until ready to serve. I stirred in the bacon pieces just before serving. They were delicious.

Very good. I made it using the skillet method of Sarah Jo. Make sure you drain almost all of the bacon grease before you put in the beans. Also, I added about twice as much broth as called for, so they would simmer better in a skillet. Also, we prefer our green beans on the softer side, so we let them cook an extra 10 minutes or so.
No changes or notes. Loved it

Made this today for Thanksgiving and it was a hit!!!! I didn't change anything except...I creased bacon by 2 strips (in addition to what recipe called for) and added half during last 10 minutes of cooking and the rest when serving. Delicious!!!!

I left out the butter completely. Chopped and fried the bacon, then in go the onions and garlic. When that's soft add the rest and let cook as long as you like. All in one pan, and even better the next day.
Super easy to make and a family favorite!
I used veggie broth, vegan butter, veganized bake non bits,
No changes needed...👍🏾 Bev
Very good! I did NOT add garlic. Everything else was delicious. I would have never thought of adding chicken broth.

One of favorites. I add more garlic. Fun memory from childhood (1960's) When my dad was in charge of lunch for us kids, he would open a can (or 2 or 3) and add a bunch of sliced hotdogs. Cook/boil until the hotdogs are done. Yummy!
Added more garlic, also left the bacon fat to sauté the onions in. I thought it was quite tasty.
